```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(htmltools)
library(fontawesome)

# get_pubs() reads publication data from a LOCAL CSV snapshot of the CV
# Google Sheet (personal_files/pubs.csv). Refresh that snapshot by running
# personal_files/pull_pubs.R (or scripts/update_site.sh) whenever the sheet
# changes. Reading locally means renders need no network and no interactive
# Google auth, so the build can't break on an expired token.
#
# If the sheet has no `country` column yet, one is added (all NA) so the
# rest of the code can rely on it existing.
get_pubs = function() {
  pubs = readr::read_csv(here::here("personal_files", "pubs.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (!"country" %in% names(pubs)) pubs$country = NA_character_
  pubs
}

# clean_summary() makes abstracts pasted from LaTeX safe for HTML.
# Pandoc silently DROPS raw LaTeX commands when the output is HTML, so
# \textit{one-to-five} would render as nothing at all. We translate the
# common commands into HTML tags before Pandoc ever sees them.
clean_summary = function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("\\\\(?:textit|emph)\\{([^}]*)\\}", "<em>\\1</em>") |>
    str_replace_all("\\\\textbf\\{([^}]*)\\}", "<strong>\\1</strong>") |>
    str_replace_all("\\\\%", "%") |>
    str_replace_all("\\\\&", "&amp;")
}

# Country names for the two-letter ISO codes used in the sheet's `country`
# column. Add a row here when a new country shows up; unknown codes fall
# back to showing the code itself.
country_names = c(
  BR = "Brazil", CO = "Colombia", ES = "Spain", ET = "Ethiopia",
  GT = "Guatemala", ID = "Indonesia", IN = "India", TW = "Taiwan",
  US = "United States", UA = "Ukraine", MX = "Mexico", PE = "Peru",
  SV = "El Salvador", HN = "Honduras", NG = "Nigeria", KE = "Kenya"
)

# flag_chip() builds the "[flag] Country" pill for one paper.
#   country: "CO", "CO, ET" (several flags in one chip), or NA -> globe icon
flag_chip = function(country) {
  if (is.na(country) || str_trim(country) == "") {
    return(paste0("<span class=\"pub-flag\">", fa("globe"), " Cross-national</span>"))
  }
  codes = str_split(country, ",")[[1]] |> str_trim() |> str_to_upper()
  # forgive common non-ISO codes typed into the sheet
  codes = dplyr::recode(codes, SP = "ES", UK = "GB")
  flags = paste0("<span class=\"fi fi-", str_to_lower(codes), "\"></span>", collapse = " ")
  names = ifelse(codes %in% names(country_names), country_names[codes], codes)
  paste0("<span class=\"pub-flag\">", flags, " ", paste(names, collapse = ", "), "</span>")
}

# render_pub() turns a data frame of publications (one row per paper) into
# HTML lists and prints them. All three sections on this page go through
# this one function, so the look is controlled in one place: the CSS block
# in the YAML header above.
#
# Columns used: title, author, url, summary, journal, pub_date, country.
#   group_by_year: print a "2026 ────" header before each year's papers
#   show_flag:     add the country chip to the meta line
#   show_venue:    add the journal / venue to the meta line
render_pub = function(pubs, group_by_year = TRUE, show_flag = TRUE, show_venue = TRUE) {
  pubs = pubs |>
    arrange(desc(pub_date)) |>
    mutate(
      year    = ifelse(is.na(pub_date), "Undated", format(pub_date, "%Y")),
      summary = clean_summary(summary),
      # bold my name in the author list
      author  = str_replace(author, "JF Tellez", "<span class=\"me\">JF Tellez</span>"),
      title_html = ifelse(
        !is.na(url),
        paste0("<a href=\"", url, "\">", title, "</a>"),
        title
      ),
      authors_html = ifelse(
        !is.na(author),
        paste0("<div class=\"pub-authors\">", author, "</div>"),
        ""
      ),
      flag_html  = if (show_flag) map_chr(country, flag_chip) else "",
      venue_html = ifelse(
        show_venue & !is.na(journal),
        paste0("<span class=\"venue\">", journal, "</span>"),
        ""
      ),
      # only print the meta line if it has something in it
      meta_html = ifelse(
        flag_html != "" | venue_html != "",
        paste0(
          "<div class=\"pub-meta\">", flag_html,
          ifelse(flag_html != "" & venue_html != "", " · ", ""),
          venue_html, "</div>"
        ),
        ""
      ),
      abstract_html = ifelse(
        !is.na(summary),
        paste0("<details><summary>Abstract</summary><p>", summary, "</p></details>"),
        ""
      ),
      item = paste0(
        "<li class=\"pub\">\n",
        "  <div class=\"pub-title\">", title_html, "</div>\n",
        "  ", authors_html, "\n",
        "  ", meta_html, "\n",
        "  ", abstract_html, "\n",
        "</li>"
      )
    )

  if (group_by_year) {
    # one <ul> per year, each preceded by a year header. Walk the years in
    # the order they already appear (newest first) -- group_by() would
    # re-sort them ascending.
    for (yr in unique(pubs$year)) {
      items = pubs$item[pubs$year == yr]
      cat(
        "<div class=\"pub-year\">", yr, "</div>\n",
        "<ul class=\"pub-list\">\n", paste(items, collapse = "\n"), "\n</ul>\n"
      )
    }
  } else {
    cat("<ul class=\"pub-list\">\n", paste(pubs$item, collapse = "\n"), "\n</ul>\n")
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

icon_link = function(icon = NULL, text = NULL, url = NULL,
                     class = "icon-link", target = "_blank") {
  if (!is.null(icon)) {
    text = HTML(paste0(tag("i", list(class = icon)), " ", text))
  }
  htmltools::a(href = url, text, class = class, target = target, rel = "noopener")
}
```

## Working papers

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}
# working papers: flat list, newest first, country flag, no venue
get_pubs() |>
  filter(category == "working_paper") |>
  render_pub(group_by_year = FALSE, show_venue = FALSE)
```


## Peer-reviewed

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}
# grouped by year, with country flag and journal
get_pubs() |>
  filter(category == "peer_reviewed") |>
  render_pub()
```


## Other writing

Book chapters, reports, blogs...

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}
# grouped by year, venue only (no country flags for this section)
get_pubs() |>
  filter(category %in% c("book_chapter", "report")) |>
  # the indicators report is intentionally left off the site
  filter(!str_detect(title, "indicators")) |>
  render_pub(show_flag = FALSE)
```
